purpose: Distinguish live neuPrint transport/API access from the prior inconclusive failures before considering large body-column scans.
assessment: A single fixed-IPv4 transport check is materially different from repeating the old unspecified address-family path. The new metadata client already used one resolved IPv4 address, a non-OSError active deadline, no environment-proxy configuration and no address fallback successfully against GCS and official documentation hosts. This does not prove that IPv6/fallback caused the previous neuPrint failures.
prior_limits: Earlier serverinfo used curl -q with5s connect/12s total timeout and got zeroHTTP/bytes at12.021380s; datasets got The read operation timed out with noHTTP at15.290041s. Receipts do not preserve the chosen address family, address attempts or detailed network stage timing; exact prior dataset client source was not retained among these files. The separate curl failure cannot be attributed to the Python alarm exception.

requests.purpose: Capture actual status and complete bounded JSON server metadata if supplied. Record public-access fields literally, with case/type and any absent fields unknown.

requests.condition: Only after request1 returns HTTP200 with complete well-formed bounded JSON. Otherwise stop after request1 without a retry.
requests.purpose: Capture complete bounded unauthenticated dataset metadata and whether the exact male-cns:v1.0 entry is present; no query/body/synapse endpoint.

pre_execution_requirements: Root approves this concrete transport experiment; freeze new client/tests/plan identities before either request.

Offline tests for complete and truncated JSON, missing/oversized Content-Length or chunked responses, error/redirect/auth statuses, total caps, non-OSError deadline, one-address connect failure with no fallback, exact second-request condition and contemporaneous source hashes.
Record address family and DNS/TCP/TLS/first-header timing, without credentials, to avoid another unsupported inference about where transport failed.
No environment proxy, credential, token/profile, browser-session or account search. No cookies or Authorization header.
Fail closed on401/403 or redirects and preserve literal response status; absent HTTP remains a host/path observation, not a claim of global service unavailability.
No automatic transition from dataset metadata to any custom query or selected-body retrieval; that requires a separate bounded decision.
